CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml) runs `cargo test --workspace` and the format-only eval script, so a green build says nothing about agent behaviour on the labeled corpus.

issues.summary: Policy-engine tests inherit ARES_KILL_SWITCH from the environment, turning 9 of 11 red when it is set
issues.suggestion: Make the kill-switch source explicit in the engine (an `EvalCtx` field or a `kill_switch: bool` parameter set from env only in `main`) and have tests pass `false`; if that is too invasive, have each test set `ARES_KILL_SWITCH=0` via a shared guard helper rather than reading ambient state.
evidence: `PolicyEngine::kill_switch_engaged` (crates/policy-engine/src/lib.rs:426) returns true when `ARES_KILL_SWITCH` is truthy, and `evaluate_inner` checks it first (line 329).
No test clears or sets the variable, so the 9 tests asserting Allow/ApprovalRequired outcomes fail with 'kill switch engaged' in any shell or CI runner that exports it.
The sibling helper crates/agent-core/src/kill.rs isolates this properly by testing only the pure `is_truthy` function, which shows the safer pattern already exists in the codebase.

issues.reasoning: Generated table from the FIRST reference implementation, fully exercised through the v40 reference-vector tests; direct tests would only duplicate upstream data.

issues.summary: api-server returns three different error-body shapes (plain text, typed ACP error, empty) despite one documented contract
issues.suggestion: Add one `ApiError` type to api-server (e.g. `(StatusCode, Json<ApiError{error: String}>)` with `impl IntoResponse`) and make every handler, including a2a's `agent_card` and `coverage`, return it; keep ACP's `{code,message,data}` only behind the `/acp` prefix where the spec requires it, and convert coverage's 'cannot read' case into a 500.
evidence: docs/services.md:37 states the contract: 'Errors: JSON `{error: string}`; 4xx = caller fixable, 5xx = retryable.'
Console/vuln/playbook handlers return `(StatusCode, String)` -> `text/plain` bodies (crates/api-server/src/main.rs:111-137, vulns.rs:49-121, playbooks.rs:70-82).
ACP handlers return `(StatusCode, Json<AcpError>)` with `{code, message, data}` (crates/api-server/src/acp.rs:51-56).
`GET /a2a/{agent}/.well-known/agent.json` returns a bare `StatusCode::NOT_FOUND` with no body (crates/api-server/src/a2a.rs:508-511).

`GET /coverage` returns HTTP 200 with a `note` field when the content directory is unreadable (crates/api-server/src/coverage.rs:22-28), so failures are indistinguishable from empty coverage without key sniffing.
Only the kill-switch handler emits an `error` key (crates/api-server/src/kill.rs:66-70), and it adds a `path` field no other endpoint has.

issues.summary: The tool-server /invoke response shape is defined three times and each client interprets it differently
issues.suggestion: Move `InvokeResponse` into `agent_protocol::tool` (next to `ToolCall`/`ToolResult`, including `approval_id`) and delete both private copies; have response-agent and detection-agent call `agent_core::HttpToolGateway` instead of hand-rolling the POST so retry and verdict handling live in one place.
evidence: Server definition with three fields: `struct InvokeResponse { decision, result, approval_id }` (crates/tool-server/src/main.rs:36-42).
Client copy A: `struct InvokeResponse { decision, result }` in agent-core (crates/agent-core/src/gateway.rs:29-32), used only inside agent-core.
Client copy B: identical duplicate in response-agent (crates/response-agent/src/main.rs:190-196) that bypasses the gateway and has no retry path.

Client C: detection-agent posts a raw `ToolCall` and treats any 2xx as success, ignoring the `decision` field (crates/detection-agent/src/pipeline.rs:248-271), contradicting the server's own header comment that 'the `decision` field is the contract, not the status code' (crates/tool-server/src/main.rs:5-7).
Because both client copies omit `approval_id`, an agent cannot tell that its call was parked for human approval instead of executed.

issues.summary: response-agent fabricates a policy Deny decision when the tool server is unreachable
issues.suggestion: Return `Result<InvokeResponse, _>` from `invoke_tool` and record an `error`/`unavailable` status in the plan step instead of inventing a `Decision`; reserve `DecisionKind::Deny` for decisions the policy engine actually rendered.
evidence: `invoke_tool` builds a fallback `Decision { kind: DecisionKind::Deny, reason: e, decided_at: Utc::now() }` for both transport and JSON-decode failures (crates/response-agent/src/main.rs:208-232).

That fabricated decision is then persisted into the plan (`"decision": invoke.decision.kind`, `"decision_reason"`, :300-304) and drives `denied = invoke.decision.kind == DecisionKind::Deny` (:290), so a network outage is recorded and acted on as an operator/policy denial.
The same 200-only contract means a real 5xx from tool-server would also be reported as a deny rather than as an unavailable dependency.

issues.summary: Tool arguments are specified twice — JSON Schema in policies/tools.yml and alias lists in executors — and no schema is exposed by the API
issues.suggestion: Add `fn schema(&self) -> Option<&serde_json::Value>` to the `Tool` trait (or have tool-server serve the policy's `args_schema`), return `[{name, schema}]` from `GET /tools`, and drop the alias lists from the executors so policy YAML is the single arg contract.
evidence: 17 tools carry `args_schema` with `additionalProperties: false` (policies/tools.yml:32-38,42-47,81-116,122-167), so only the canonical key names can ever reach an executor.

Executors nonetheless accept undocumented aliases: `arg_str(args, &["value", "ioc", "query"])` (executors/mod.rs:190), `&["case_id", "id"]` (:126), `&["q", "query_string"]` (:97), `&["cve_id", "id", "cve"]` (:583), plus shape polymorphism ('`{case_id, observable}` or flat fields', :131-136) and `values` vs `value` fallbacks (:280-296).
The trait exposes no schema: `fn name()` + `async fn execute(&self, args: &Value)` (executors/mod.rs:36-38).

`GET /tools` returns names only (`Json<Vec<String>>`, crates/tool-server/src/main.rs:208), and `PolicyEngine` keeps validators private, exposing only `tool_names()` (crates/policy-engine/src/lib.rs:305).

issues.summary: Rate-limit classifier covers /a2a twins but never matches /acp, so ACP runs fall into the general tier
issues.suggestion: Classify by prefix once — e.g. match `/a2a/` and `/acp/` together for `Expensive` and both `.../events` suffixes for `Stream` — and add an `/acp/runs` assertion to the existing `classify_maps_paths_to_tiers` test.
evidence: `classify` maps `POST /cvss/score` and `path.starts_with("/a2a/")` to `Tier::Expensive` and `/a2a/tasks/*/events` to `Tier::Stream` (crates/api-server/src/ratelimit.rs:30,38).

No branch matches `/acp/`, so `POST /acp/runs` (same agents, same NATS publish, same LLM cost) and `GET /acp/runs/{id}/events` (a long-lived SSE) are metered as `Tier::General` (defaults 60/s, burst 120) instead of `expensive`/`stream`.
The router mounts both families in one table (crates/api-server/src/main.rs:326-338), so adding a protocol front silently inherits the wrong limits.

issues.summary: PolicyEngine::evaluate and evaluate_approved are async but perform no async work, forcing callers to hold a mutex across an await
issues.suggestion: Make `evaluate`/`evaluate_approved` synchronous (`fn evaluate(&self, call, ctx) -> Decision`), drop the `.await` at both call sites, and remove `Mutex<EvalCtx>` from `AppState` so concurrent invokes stop serializing on policy evaluation.
evidence: `pub async fn evaluate(&self, call: &ToolCall, ctx: &mut EvalCtx) -> Decision` (crates/policy-engine/src/lib.rs:314) and `evaluate_approved` (:331) both delegate to the synchronous `fn evaluate_inner(...)` (:344) with no `.await` anywhere in the chain.

Callers therefore wrap the context in `tokio::sync::Mutex<EvalCtx>` and hold the guard across the await: `let mut ctx = state.eval_ctx.lock().await; state.engine.evaluate(&call, &mut ctx).await` (crates/tool-server/src/main.rs:84-87, repeated in approvals.rs:242-245).
`EvalCtx` already holds `Arc<DashMap<String, u32>>` counters (crates/policy-engine/src/lib.rs:46-48), so the outer mutex is the only reason evaluations serialize.

issues.summary: AuditWriter::append takes six positional parameters, four of them adjacent &str, and takes the decision as a string
issues.suggestion: Replace the parameter list with one struct — `AuditEntry { actor, tool, args, decision: DecisionKind, reason, correlation_id }` — so the compiler enforces field names and the enum, and delete `decision_label` from the call sites.
evidence: `pub async fn append(&self, actor: &str, tool: &str, args: &Value, decision: &str, reason: &str, correlation_id: Uuid)` (crates/audit/src/lib.rs:59-67) — six parameters, with `actor`/`tool`/`decision`/`reason` all plain `&str`.

Callers must pre-convert the domain enum: `decision_label(&decision.kind)` at crates/tool-server/src/main.rs:90-98, and the reject path hardcodes the literal `"deny"` (crates/tool-server/src/approvals.rs:349).
Transposing `decision` and `reason` compiles silently and corrupts the hash-chained row; the audit table is the tamper-evident record, so a mis-order is unrecoverable.

issues.summary: POST /controls/kill-switch silently engages on a malformed body and returns different fields than the GET
issues.suggestion: Return `400 {error}` when a non-empty body fails to parse, and have GET and POST emit the identical `{engaged, state}` object.
evidence: `serde_json::from_slice::<KillBody>(&body).map(|b| b.engaged).unwrap_or(true)` (crates/api-server/src/kill.rs:41-46) — any malformed or misspelled payload engages the kill switch instead of returning 400.

GET returns `{"engaged": bool}` (crates/api-server/src/kill.rs:37-39) while POST returns `{"state": "engaged"|"disengaged", "engaged": bool}` (:62-64), so a client that round-trips the same resource must handle two shapes.
The error branch returns `{"error", "path"}` (:66-70), a fourth body shape in the same file.

issues.summary: Two public enrichment entry points with conflicting error contracts; the Result-returning one can never fail and has no callers
issues.suggestion: Delete the free `enrich` wrapper, and either return `Result<Vec<EnrichmentResult>>` from the method or add an explicit `partial: bool`/`failed_providers` field to the result so callers can tell 'no intel' from 'no providers reachable'.
evidence: `Enricher::enrich(&self, ioc: &str) -> Vec<EnrichmentResult>` is infallible: provider errors are logged and skipped, so an all-providers-down run is indistinguishable from a clean miss (crates/enrichment-lib/src/lib.rs:231-259).

`pub async fn enrich(enricher: &Enricher, ioc: &str) -> Result<Vec<EnrichmentResult>>` wraps it as `Ok(...)` unconditionally (crates/enrichment-lib/src/lib.rs:520-522), advertising a failure mode that cannot occur.
The free function has no callers — triage-agent calls the method directly (crates/triage-agent/src/main.rs:279).

issues.summary: MispClient search methods silently discard rows that fail to deserialize, so malformed data looks like 'no results'
issues.suggestion: Use `serde_json::from_value::<Event>(...)?` (or `collect::<Result<Vec<_>,_>>()`) so a schema mismatch surfaces as an error, or log-and-count skipped rows into a returned struct.
evidence: `search` drops any event whose payload does not deserialize: `if let Ok(e) = serde_json::from_value::<Event>(ev.clone())` (crates/connectors/src/lib.rs:468-472).
`search_attributes` does the same via `filter_map(|r| serde_json::from_value(r.clone()).ok())` (:509-514).

Both return `Result<Vec<_>>`, so the signature promises the error channel exists while the implementation swallows the exact failure it would report; callers such as the `misp.search` executor (crates/tool-server/src/executors/mod.rs:184-192) get an empty vector and report a clean 'no intel' answer.

issues.summary: All three HTTP services accept anonymous requests; the only gate is per-tool policy
issues.suggestion: Add one shared tower layer (e.g. a `require_bearer` from_fn in a new `crates/http-auth` or in `http-limits`) that validates a token from env/secret and rejects with 401, then apply it to api_router(), tool-server's Router and ingestion-gateway's Router next to the existing rate-limit layer; stop publishing 8090/8091 to the host until it exists.
evidence: crates/api-server/src/main.rs:283-325 lists 27 routes including POST /controls/kill-switch, POST /a2a/{agent}, POST /acp/runs and GET /audit; main.rs:361-367 applies only http_limits::middleware and CorsLayer::permissive().
crates/tool-server/src/main.rs:274-281 serves /invoke, /tools and /approvals/{id}/approve|reject with no authentication; infra/docker-compose.yml:330 publishes 8090:8090 to the host.
crates/api-server/src/ratelimit.rs:3-5 and crates/http-limits/src/lib.rs:10-12 both document keys as 'peer IP until authentication lands'.
docs/services.md:119 states no endpoint in any of the three services performs authentication or authorization today.

issues.summary: A2A agent cards advertise bearer auth that the server never enforces
issues.suggestion: Either enforce the advertised scheme (reject requests without a valid Authorization: Bearer at rpc_endpoint) or remove the `authentication` claim so the card does not promise a trust boundary the service does not have.
evidence: crates/api-server/src/a2a.rs:158-160 sets Authentication { schemes: vec!["bearer"] } for every agent card built by card_for().
crates/api-server/src/a2a.rs:189-191 sets the same scheme on the platform card returned by /.well-known/agent.json.
crates/api-server/src/a2a.rs:515-532 rpc_endpoint deserializes the body and dispatches without inspecting any header.

issues.summary: Global kill switch: no auth, no audit row, and the file it writes is not the one policy reads
issues.suggestion: Gate the POST behind the shared auth layer, append an audit_log event with the caller identity on every engage/disengage, and propagate state through one channel the enforcer reads (a NATS control subject or a writable shared volume), not a per-container file.
evidence: crates/api-server/src/kill.rs:39-72 writes or removes $POLICIES_DIR/kill from an unauthenticated POST, taking the body as raw Bytes and defaulting an empty body to engaged=true.
No actor is captured and no audit_log row is written, while every tool decision is appended to the hash chain (crates/tool-server/src/main.rs:82-99).

infra/docker-compose.yml:311-330 mounts ../policies:/policies:ro into tool-server, but api-server (:341-348) has no policies mount, so its write lands in its own container filesystem and policy-engine's read at crates/policy-engine/src/lib.rs:452 never sees it.
crates/policy-engine/src/lib.rs:443-456 also honours ARES_KILL_SWITCH, giving two independent switch states with no reconciliation.

issues.summary: Four agents reach side effects outside the policy engine while the same tools are allowlisted
issues.suggestion: Route each of these effects through HttpToolGateway so the allowlist is the single decision point — delete the direct ThehiveClient calls in triage/hunt, replace detection-agent's promote/deploy_monitor with a real `detection.sigma.deploy` executor that performs the effect, and make bas-runner invoke exec.bas.run — or delete the now-dead allowlist entries so the policy file stops implying coverage it does not provide.
evidence: crates/triage-agent/src/main.rs:186 and crates/hunt-agent/src/main.rs:125 call ThehiveClient::create_case directly, although thehive.case.create is allowlisted (policies/tools.yml:14) with a real executor (crates/tool-server/src/executors/mod.rs:678).

crates/detection-agent/src/main.rs:193-195 runs promote_and_commit (file move + git commit) and deploy_monitor (OpenSearch monitor POST with basic auth) before calling detection.sigma.deploy, whose executor is a DryRun (crates/tool-server/src/executors/mod.rs:769-772); the policy verdict is only logged (crates/detection-agent/src/pipeline.rs:266-268).

crates/bas-runner/src/main.rs:86-116 spawns ssh/winrm for scenario commands with no policy evaluation and no kill-switch check, even though exec.bas.run is registered behind OpenShell (crates/tool-server/src/executors/mod.rs:775-781).
Only response-agent (crates/response-agent/src/main.rs:280-291) and agent-core (crates/agent-core/src/agent_loop.rs:148-158) route every effect through the gateway.

issues.summary: Approver identity comes from the request body and defaults to 'operator'; no separation of duties
issues.suggestion: Derive the approver from the authenticated principal (the same middleware that fixes the authn gap) instead of the body, reject approve/reject when no principal is present, and refuse an approval whose principal equals call.actor to enforce separation of duties.
evidence: crates/tool-server/src/approvals.rs:213-216 reads `approver` from the optional JSON body and falls back to "operator".
crates/tool-server/src/approvals.rs:276-279 does the same for reject.
The resulting string is written as the audit actor (approvals.rs:248-255 for approve, 299-308 for reject), so the human-approval record proves only that someone reached an unauthenticated port.
Nothing compares the approver with the parked call's own `actor`, so the caller that submitted a call can approve it.

issues.summary: ToolCall.actor is caller-supplied and ignored by the policy engine, so authz is per-tool only
issues.suggestion: Resolve the actor from the authenticated caller in the tool-server middleware and overwrite call.actor before evaluation, then add a per-actor rule to policies/tools.yml (e.g. an `actors:` map with allowed tool prefixes) so a compromised agent cannot invoke another agent's tools.
evidence: crates/agent-protocol/src/tool.rs:19 defines actor as a plain String supplied by the caller.

crates/policy-engine/src/lib.rs:344-440 evaluates kill switch, allowlist, autonomy, schema, forbidden args, protected assets and blast radius — the actor is never consulted, and policies/tools.yml has no per-actor section.

Actor literals are hardcoded per crate ("response-agent" at crates/response-agent/src/main.rs:284, "detection-agent" at crates/detection-agent/src/pipeline.rs:258, "agent-core" at crates/agent-core/src/agent_loop.rs:152) with no shared constant, and "agent-core" is not one of the agents listed in crates/api-server/src/a2a.rs:76-125.
Because tool-server is unauthenticated, the actor recorded in the audit chain is whatever the client typed.

issues.summary: tasks/get and tasks/cancel ignore the addressed agent, so any agent path reaches any task
issues.suggestion: Add `agent: &str` to TaskBackend::get/cancel, pass the path segment in dispatch, and constrain the SQL with `AND agent = $2` (returning None on mismatch) so a task is only reachable through the agent it was sent to.
evidence: crates/a2a/src/rpc.rs:144-148 declares TaskBackend::get(task_id) and cancel(task_id) with no agent parameter.
crates/a2a/src/rpc.rs:158-172 dispatches METHOD_GET and METHOD_CANCEL without passing the `agent` path segment it received.
crates/api-server/src/a2a.rs:478-494 loads and cancels the row by id alone, so POST /a2a/hunt-agent with a triage-agent task id reads or cancels it.
crates/a2a/src/rpc.rs:153-156 documents that 'the backend validates that it is a known agent', which is only true for send.

issues.summary: ACP run creation and SSE streams fall into the general rate tier while their A2A twins are throttled
issues.suggestion: Extend classify() with the ACP twins: `path.starts_with("/acp/runs")` for POST -> Tier::Expensive and `path.ends_with("/events")` for GET -> Tier::Stream, and add the two new cases to the classify_maps_paths_to_tiers test.
evidence: crates/api-server/src/ratelimit.rs:34-41 assigns Tier::Expensive to POST /cvss/score and any path starting with /a2a/, but not to POST /acp/runs, POST /acp/runs/{id}/cancel or POST /acp/runs/{id}.

crates/api-server/src/ratelimit.rs:27-33 assigns Tier::Stream to /stream/activity and /a2a/tasks/*/events, but GET /acp/runs/{id}/events falls through to Tier::General, losing both the concurrency cap and the stream exemption from request counting.
Both surfaces dispatch the same agent work through the same NATS publish path (crates/api-server/src/acp.rs:236-247 and crates/api-server/src/a2a.rs:434-451).

issues.summary: Every service uses one owner Postgres role; no RLS anywhere and the audit chain is never verified
issues.suggestion: Create per-service Postgres roles at bootstrap with GRANT INSERT/SELECT only on audit_log (no UPDATE/DELETE) and enable RLS on the per-run tables keyed by service role, then add a verify() that re-walks audit_log hash links and expose it through GET /audit so tampering is actually detectable.
evidence: The blind packet reports 7 tables (a2a_tasks, agent_checkpoints, bas_results, response_actions, seen_alerts, tool_idempotency, vuln_advisories) and zero with RLS; each table is created ad hoc by whichever service owns it (e.g. crates/api-server/src/a2a.rs:207-230, crates/tool-server/src/idempotency.rs:125-133).
Every service connects with the same DATABASE_URL (crates/tool-server/src/main.rs:236-248, crates/api-server/src/main.rs:334), so any of them can UPDATE or DELETE audit_log rows the others wrote.
crates/audit/src/lib.rs:59-115 writes prev_hash/hash but no code anywhere re-walks the chain to detect tampering (no reader beyond api-server's plain SELECT at crates/api-server/src/main.rs:187-197).
infra/helm/ares/templates/postgres.yaml provisions a single POSTGRES_USER with no per-service roles.

issues.summary: Reject path hardcodes the "deny" decision label instead of the shared decision_label()
issues.suggestion: Replace the literal with crate::decision_label(&DecisionKind::Deny) so both approval outcomes go through the single label function.
evidence: crates/tool-server/src/main.rs:63-69 centralizes the audit vocabulary in decision_label().
crates/tool-server/src/approvals.rs:252 calls crate::decision_label(&decision.kind) on approve, but approvals.rs:304 passes the literal "deny" on reject.
The label is a query key for audit_log rows (crates/api-server/src/main.rs:187-197 returns `decision` verbatim), so a typo or rename in one path silently splits the audit vocabulary.

issues.summary: ActivityEvent + emit() copy-pasted into five agent crates, and the copy has already drifted
issues.suggestion: Move `ActivityEvent`, `SUBJECT_ACTIVITY` and the `publish_activity(nats, &event)` helper into agent-core (already a dependency of triage, response, vuln) and delete the five copies; give vuln-agent the shared event so its `workflow_run_id` is populated. Do not add a new crate for this.
evidence: Five near-identical `activity.rs` files (detection 41, hunt 41, response 41, triage 44 LOC) declare the same `SUBJECT_ACTIVITY` const and the same `ActivityEvent { workflow_run_id, agent, step, detail, ts }` struct.
`async fn emit(client, event)` is byte-identical in detection-agent/src/main.rs:72-84, hunt-agent/src/main.rs:55-67, response-agent/src/main.rs:86-98 and triage-agent/src/main.rs:79-91.
Drift: triage-agent/src/activity.rs:22 declares `step: &'static str` while the other four take `String`; triage adds a module comment defending the duplication ('The shape is defined locally here').

Worse drift: vuln-agent/src/main.rs:120-135 hand-builds `json!({agent, step, detail, ts})` with no `workflow_run_id`, so its events can never match the filter `v.get("workflow_run_id") != Some(run_id)` at api-server/src/a2a.rs:610 and acp.rs:559 — vuln progress silently never reaches the console SSE.

Each agent's `while let Some(msg) = sub.next().await { tokio::spawn(...) }` + `info_span!` + envelope-parse block is also copy-pasted (detection:258-278, hunt:222-246, response:409-427, triage main loop).

issues.summary: agent-core ships ~545 LOC of framework (AgentLoop, HttpToolGateway, CheckpointStore, Budgets) that no binary instantiates
issues.suggestion: Either wire the agents through `AgentLoop`/`HttpToolGateway` (making checkpoints real and deleting the per-agent invoke code), or delete agent_loop.rs, gateway.rs, checkpoint.rs and budget.rs and keep agent-core to kill.rs + state.rs. The middle state — published framework nothing calls, plus read paths that can never fire — is the expensive one.
evidence: grep for `agent_core::` outside the crate returns only `kill_switch_engaged` (api-server/main.rs:39, kill.rs:9, response-agent:22, triage-agent:24, vuln-agent:18) and the `AgentState`/`Step` types read by api-server (a2a.rs:320-329, acp.rs:159-167).
