evidence: Doc: '`GET /rest/json/cves/2.0?cveId=` — one CVE by ID, `None` when NVD has no record (unknown, reserved-and-unpublished, or rejected IDs may 404 or return an empty list)' (crates/connectors/src/lib.rs:954-957)

The shared `get` only retries 403/429/5xx and bails on anything else with `anyhow::bail!("NVD HTTP {status}")`, so a 404 becomes `Err` before get_cve can return None (crates/connectors/src/lib.rs:919-941)

Enricher::enrich_cve negative-caches only the `Ok(None)` arm for 1h (crates/enrichment-lib/src/lib.rs:459-466); the 404 path takes the `Err` arm (467-471) and is not cached, contradicting the doc's 'so rejected/reserved IDs don't hammer the rate limit'

issues.summary: The 'hash-chained' audit log reads prev_hash then inserts without a lock, so concurrent appends fork the chain
issues.suggestion: Take a transaction-scoped lock around the read+insert (e.g. `SELECT pg_advisory_xact_lock(...)` in the same tx as the INSERT, or a single INSERT ... SELECT that derives prev_hash from the last row) so the chain stays linear; note the single-writer assumption in the docstring otherwise.
evidence: Module doc: 'writes a hash-chained AuditEvent ... forming a tamper-evident chain in audit_log' (crates/audit/src/lib.rs:1-11); append documents 'reads the previous event's hash ... chains hash = sha256(prev_hash || canonical fields), inserts the row' (53-57)
The read (`SELECT hash FROM audit_log ORDER BY seq DESC LIMIT 1`) and the insert are separate statements with no transaction, advisory lock or serializable isolation (crates/audit/src/lib.rs:70-101)

Callers append per request with no mutual exclusion — every `POST /invoke` audits independently (crates/tool-server/src/main.rs:82-99) — so two concurrent decisions can both chain onto the same prev_hash and produce two children

issues.summary: A2A SSE writes task state 'completed' for every terminal step, including kill-switch halts and rejected detections
issues.suggestion: Map the terminal step to the right TaskState (kill_switch → canceled/failed, rejected → failed) or write 'completed' only for the genuine success steps ('deployed', 'close', 'done'), keeping the SSE close behavior unchanged.
evidence: terminal_step() treats triage/response 'kill_switch' and detection 'rejected' as work finished (crates/api-server/src/a2a.rs:127-137)
On any such step the SSE generator unconditionally runs `UPDATE a2a_tasks SET state = 'completed'` (crates/api-server/src/a2a.rs:615-623)

TaskState::Completed is documented as 'The task finished successfully' and Canceled as 'The task was canceled before completion' (crates/a2a/src/task.rs:24-31); a kill-switch halt or a noisy-rule rejection is neither, so tasks/get then reports success for a run that was stopped

issues.summary: Status::Approved is documented as 'approved and the call was executed' but is set before the post-approval policy re-check
issues.suggestion: Either add a distinct terminal status for 'approved but blocked by re-check' (or set Rejected/Failed when the re-check denies), or soften the doc to 'a human approved and execution was attempted'.
evidence: Status::Approved doc: 'A human approved and the call was executed' (crates/tool-server/src/approvals.rs:39-40)
approve() settles the record to Approved first (218-227) and only then re-evaluates policy (230-233); when the re-check returns Deny the result is a failure stub and nothing executes (235-243)
The record keeps status Approved with an error result, so `GET /approvals?status=approved` lists calls that were never performed

issues.summary: severity_from_level documents clamping out-of-range levels but silently downgrades them to 'medium'
issues.suggestion: Clamp both ends — `SEVERITY_LEVELS.get(level.round().clamp(0.0, 3.0) as usize)` — so an out-of-range high level resolves to 'critical', matching the docstring.
evidence: Doc: 'Maps a decision-model severity level (0–3, probability-weighted) to the verdict severity label, clamping out-of-range values' (crates/triage-agent/src/main.rs:147-149)
Implementation clamps only the low end (`level.round().max(0.0)`) and falls back to "medium" when the index is out of range (149-155), so a level of 4.0 yields 'medium' instead of the top band
The downgrade is behavioral: severity_gte_high() then suppresses the handoff to response-agent for an alert the model scored at maximum severity (66-68, 439-447)

issues.summary: The registry test claims startup aborts on a missing executor, but main only logs a warning
issues.suggestion: Pick one contract: either fail boot on a non-empty missing list (`anyhow::ensure!`) or reword the test doc and missing_executors doc to say the check is advisory and logged.
evidence: Test doc: 'Every tool named in `policies/tools.yml` must have an executor, or startup aborts (`missing_executors` in main)' (crates/tool-server/src/executors/mod.rs:803-805)
main() computes missing_executors and only `warn!(?missing, "allowlisted tools have no executor")` before serving (crates/tool-server/src/main.rs:231-234)
missing_executors' own doc calls itself a 'startup sanity check' (crates/tool-server/src/executors/mod.rs:787-797), reinforcing the abort expectation

issues.summary: RunMode::Sync promises to block until a terminal state, but api-server returns after 120s with a non-terminal run and HTTP 200
issues.suggestion: Document the timeout in the RunMode::Sync contract (e.g. 'blocks until terminal or SYNC_TIMEOUT, returning the live run') or return 202 instead of 200 when the timeout elapses so the wire response matches the promised semantics.
evidence: RunMode::Sync doc: 'Block until the run reaches a terminal state' (crates/acp/src/lib.rs:186-190)

api-server wraps the wait in `tokio::time::timeout(SYNC_TIMEOUT, ...)` and ignores the elapsed result, then returns whatever state the row is in with StatusCode::OK (crates/api-server/src/acp.rs:47-48, 185-218, 390-395)
A client following the type contract cannot distinguish 'finished' from 'still running' without re-reading `status`

issues.summary: JsonRpcRequest.jsonrpc is documented as always "2.0" and INVALID_REQUEST is documented, but neither is ever enforced or emitted
issues.suggestion: Validate `req.jsonrpc == "2.0"` in dispatch and return INVALID_REQUEST when it is not, or drop the constant and reword the field doc so the API does not advertise an unenforced contract.
evidence: `pub jsonrpc: String` is documented as 'The JSON-RPC version string (`"2.0"`)' (crates/a2a/src/rpc.rs:33-37) yet dispatch() never reads it (157-209)

INVALID_REQUEST is a documented public constant — 'the payload is not a well-formed JSON-RPC request' (crates/a2a/src/rpc.rs:22-23) — with no producer anywhere in the workspace; a request with `jsonrpc: "1.0"` is accepted and answered as 2.0

issues.summary: load_playbooks documents that unparseable files are 'reported in errors', but both handlers discard the list
issues.suggestion: Return `{"playbooks": [...], "errors": [...]}` from list_playbooks (matching coverage.rs) or delete the errors vec and its doc line so the function contract matches what it delivers.
evidence: Doc: 'Unparseable files are skipped and reported in `errors`' (crates/api-server/src/playbooks.rs:16-18), and the function accumulates them (52-57)
Both public handlers bind the result to `_errors` and return only the array (69-73) or a single document (75-83), so the reporting never reaches a caller
Coverage's sibling endpoint surfaces its equivalent list under `errors` (crates/api-server/src/coverage.rs:57-61), which makes the playbook silence look like an oversight rather than a choice

issues.summary: rollback_for maps reversible actions to tool names that exist in no allowlist or registry, so every recorded rollback is undispatchable
issues.suggestion: Either register and allowlist the inverse tools (blocklist.ip.remove, wazuh.active_response.unisolate_host, entra.user.enable, ad.user.enable, firewall.rule.remove, o365.email.release, misp.ioc.unblock) so the stored rollback entries are dispatchable, or drop rollback_for and the rollback_json column until the inverse tools exist, and correct docs/services.md so it does not promise compensation the code cannot perform.
evidence: crates/response-agent/src/main.rs:104-130 returns rollback tools such as "blocklist.ip.remove", "wazuh.active_response.unisolate_host", "entra.user.enable", "ad.user.enable", "firewall.rule.remove", "o365.email.release", "misp.ioc.unblock".
grep across the repo finds those names only in that function and in docs/services.md:65; policies/tools.yml lists 41 tools and none of the *remove/enable/unblock/unisolate/release variants.
executors::build_registry (crates/tool-server/src/executors/mod.rs:660-780) registers no such executor, so a rollback call would be denied by PolicyEngine as "tool not in allowlist" before dispatch.
Nothing consumes `rollback_json` except the read-model SELECT at crates/api-server/src/main.rs:261, so the compensation path described in docs/services.md:64-67 never runs.

issues.summary: --dry skips execution but still records detected=false rows and publishes coverage-gap envelopes that trigger detection-agent
issues.suggestion: Return early from run_scenario when `deps.dry` is true (or when execute reported a dry run) so no bas_results rows are written and no SUBJECT_DETECTION envelope is published; alternatively tag the payload/row with `dry_run=true` and have the detection-agent filter on it.
evidence: crates/bas-runner/src/main.rs:93-99: `execute` logs and returns Ok(()) when the transport env var is unset or `dry` is true.

crates/bas-runner/src/main.rs:186-243: run_scenario proceeds regardless of `deps.dry`, waits up to 600s for MTTD, inserts one `bas_results` row per technique with `detected=false`, and republishes the payload to SUBJECT_DETECTION when `!detected`.
The module doc (lines 15-17) describes dry mode as 'the run is a logged dry run', i.e. no results are implied.

issues.summary: PolicyEngine::evaluate and evaluate_approved are async but only call the synchronous evaluate_inner, forcing pointless awaits
issues.suggestion: Make evaluate/evaluate_approved synchronous (drop `async`) and update the two call sites; if the blocking kill-file read must stay, note it explicitly or move the check to a cached value refreshed off the request path.
evidence: crates/policy-engine/src/lib.rs:314-326 and :331-343 declare `pub async fn evaluate` / `evaluate_approved` whose bodies contain no `.await`.
Both delegate to the synchronous `fn evaluate_inner` (line 342), so the futures never suspend.

Callers must await while holding the shared context lock: crates/tool-server/src/main.rs:96-98 and crates/tool-server/src/approvals.rs:242-244 both do `state.eval_ctx.lock().await` then `engine.evaluate(...).await`.
`kill_switch_engaged` inside evaluate_inner does blocking `std::fs::read_to_string` (line 443-457) inside what looks like an async path.

issues.summary: The retry loop re-checks try_clone() after the function already returned when the body is not replayable, making the loop's error branch unreachable
issues.suggestion: Delete the in-loop `try_clone` guard and clone unconditionally (or hoist one clone before the loop); keep the single early guard as the only place that decides replayability.
evidence: crates/connectors/src/lib.rs:80-83: if `req.try_clone().is_none()` the function sends once and returns, so a non-cloneable builder can never reach the loop.

crates/connectors/src/lib.rs:87-89: inside the loop, `let Some(attempt_req) = req.try_clone() else { return Err(anyhow!("request body cannot be replayed")) }` can therefore never fire; `req` is never consumed (only its clones are sent).
The same condition is handled two different ways in one function (single send vs. hard error), which is what makes the dead arm confusing.

issues.summary: cancel_run's `rows_affected() == 0` early return is textually identical to the fall-through tail, so the guard changes nothing
issues.suggestion: Drop the `if updated.rows_affected() == 0 { ... }` block and rely on the single trailing load_run/404 path (the UPDATE result is only needed if you intend different status codes for 'already terminal' vs 'just cancelled').
evidence: crates/api-server/src/acp.rs:459-472 returns `load_run(...).map(...ACCEPTED...).ok_or_else(404)` when the UPDATE matched no row.
crates/api-server/src/acp.rs:473-484 repeats the exact same expression unconditionally, so the early return is dead weight and a reader must diff two 14-line blocks to see they agree.

issues.summary: Deps.os is never read but its construction makes OPENSEARCH_URL mandatory at boot
issues.suggestion: Delete the `os` field and its construction from Deps; `os_url` already carries the only OpenSearch information the agent uses, so the startup requirement disappears with it.
evidence: crates/triage-agent/src/main.rs:339-342 carries `#[allow(dead_code)] os: Arc<OpensearchClient>` with the comment 'kept for parity with the connector config'.

crates/triage-agent/src/main.rs:480-484 builds it with `.context("OPENSEARCH_URL not set")?`, so the process refuses to start without an env var that no code path uses (verdict writes go through `http`/`os_url`, which has a localhost default).
`process` and `open_case` take `&Deps` and never touch `os`, confirming the field is inert.

issues.summary: load_playbooks collects parse errors and both handlers immediately discard them, so broken playbook files are invisible
issues.suggestion: Either return the errors in the response body (`{"playbooks": [...], "errors": [...]}`) so a developer sees why a file vanished, or change load_playbooks to log via tracing and remove the unused error vector.
evidence: crates/api-server/src/playbooks.rs:24-27 documents that unparseable files are 'skipped and reported in `errors`'.
crates/api-server/src/playbooks.rs:71 and :77 both bind `let (playbooks, _errors) = load_playbooks();` and drop the error vector, so `GET /playbooks` silently returns a short list.
The `Err` arm at :53-56 and the 'cannot read {dir}' arm at :36-39 therefore write into a channel with no reader.

issues.summary: AuditWriter::ship (OpenSearch mirroring promised by the module doc) has no callers, and append's read-then-insert can fork the hash chain
issues.suggestion: Call `ship` after a successful append (log-and-continue on failure), or delete it and the doc sentence; and make the chain read+insert atomic, e.g. `INSERT ... SELECT` with the previous hash computed in one statement plus a unique index on (prev_hash) or an advisory lock.
evidence: crates/audit/src/lib.rs:3-5 states that `ship` mirrors each event into OpenSearch `ares-audit` for SIEM visibility; grep for `.ship(` across the workspace returns zero call sites.
crates/tool-server/src/main.rs:99-112 only calls `writer.append(...)`, so no audit event ever reaches OpenSearch.

crates/audit/src/lib.rs:79-92 reads `SELECT hash ... ORDER BY seq DESC LIMIT 1` and then inserts in a separate statement with no transaction or lock, so two concurrent /invoke calls can both chain onto the same prev_hash and fork the tamper-evident chain.

issues.summary: An unrecognised VULN_MIN_SEVERITY ranks 0, which makes the severity filter always true instead of failing
issues.suggestion: Parse `min_severity` once at startup into a validated enum (clap `value_parser` or a `match` returning an error) and abort boot on an unknown value, so the comparison can never degrade to `>= 0`.
evidence: crates/vuln-agent/src/main.rs:86-94: `severity_rank` returns 0 for any unknown string.

crates/vuln-agent/src/main.rs:221-228: `min_rank = severity_rank(&cfg.min_severity)` and `qualifies = severity_rank(&severity) >= min_rank || rec.has_kev || matched.is_some()`; with a typo such as `VULN_MIN_SEVERITY=hgih` every CVE (rank >= 0) qualifies and cases are opened for the whole NVD window.
The clap arg at :64-66 is a free-form String, so nothing rejects the typo earlier.

issues.summary: JsonRpcRequest.jsonrpc is parsed but never checked and the INVALID_REQUEST error code is never emitted
issues.suggestion: Add a leading guard in `dispatch`: `if req.jsonrpc != "2.0" { return JsonRpcResponse::err(id, INVALID_REQUEST, format!("unsupported jsonrpc: {}", req.jsonrpc)) }`, which also makes the existing constant live.
evidence: crates/a2a/src/rpc.rs:33-38 declares `jsonrpc: String` with the doc 'The JSON-RPC version string ("2.0")'.
crates/a2a/src/rpc.rs:152-215 `dispatch` matches only on `req.method`; `req.jsonrpc` is never read, so `{"jsonrpc":"1.0",...}` is served as valid.
crates/a2a/src/rpc.rs:22-23 defines `INVALID_REQUEST = -32600`, which grep shows is never used anywhere in the workspace (dead constant that documents a check nobody wrote).

issues.summary: forbidden_args classes are raw strings matched with `_ => false`, so a typo silently disables the IP-class check
issues.suggestion: Add `#[derive(Deserialize)] #[serde(rename_all = "...")] enum IpClass { Rfc1918, Loopback, Multicast, LinkLocal, Unspecified, Cgnat }`, type `forbidden_args: HashMap<String, Vec<IpClass>>`, and match on the enum exhaustively — an unknown class in tools.yml then fails `PolicyEngine::load` instead of quietly allowing the call.
evidence: crates/policy-engine/src/lib.rs:521-537 dispatches on class name literals ("RFC1918", "loopback", "multicast", "link_local", "unspecified", "cgNAT"/"shared") and returns `false` for anything else, so the check passes by default.
policies/tools.yml:129-130 supplies those names as free-form YAML (`ip: [RFC1918, loopback, multicast]`); `PolicyEngine::load` (lib.rs:268-301) never validates them.
The same file already types the sibling policy fields as serde enums (`Impact`, `Autonomy` at lib.rs:67-82), so the stricter pattern is right there.

issues.summary: AuditEvent.decision is a String re-derived from DecisionKind by hand and written with raw literals on the approval path
issues.suggestion: Type the field as `DecisionKind` (or a dedicated `AuditDecision` enum covering the approval/rejection paths), delete `decision_label`, pass `decision.kind` into `AuditWriter::append`, and add a `#[derive(sqlx::FromRow)]` audit row so `GET /audit` returns the enum rather than untyped JSON.
evidence: crates/agent-protocol/src/audit.rs:25 declares `pub decision: String` even though `DecisionKind` (tool.rs:27-36) is the type that owns those values and already serializes snake_case.

crates/tool-server/src/main.rs:62-69 hand-rolls `decision_label()` to reproduce that serialization; crates/tool-server/src/approvals.rs:300 bypasses it entirely with the literal "deny" when a human rejects a call.
No reader sees a type: crates/bas-runner/src/main.rs:155 filters `decision = 'allow'` in SQL and crates/api-server/src/main.rs:187-198 returns `to_jsonb(t)` rows as `Vec<Value>`.

issues.summary: Severity is a bare string in six modules with two fail-open rank parsers, so a config typo escalates every CVE
issues.suggestion: Define one `Severity` enum (None/Low/Medium/High/Critical) with serde spellings and a `rank()`/`Ord` impl, parse the CLI/env threshold into it with clap `ValueEnum`, and replace `severity_rank`, `severity_gte_high` and the `open_case` match with the enum so invalid input fails at startup instead of becoming rank 0.
evidence: Two spellings of the same band: crates/cvss/src/lib.rs:44,53 yields `severity: &'static str` ("None"/"Low"/"Medium"/"High"/"Critical") while crates/connectors/src/lib.rs:825 keeps NVD's `Option<String>` ("HIGH").

crates/vuln-agent/src/main.rs:53 types the threshold as `String` and :86-94 maps it with `_ => 0`, so `VULN_MIN_SEVERITY=hgih` makes `severity_rank(&severity) >= min_rank` (:228) true for every CVE with a metric.
The same rank is written into `NewCase.severity: u8` (:258); an unrecognised band sends TheHive severity 0, outside its 1-4 range.

crates/triage-agent/src/main.rs:60,66-68,256-261 adds a third mapping (`severity_gte_high`, the `open_case` match with `_ => 2`) and crates/api-server/src/vulns.rs:36-38 accepts `cvss_v4_severity`/`cvss_v3_severity` as free strings that are just uppercased.

issues.summary: LLM verdict/severity are String fields matched against literals, and an unexpected value silently drops the alert
issues.suggestion: Deserialize into `enum Verdict { Tp, Fp, Suspicious }` and `enum Severity` with `#[serde(rename_all = "lowercase")]`; a hallucinated label then fails `serde_json::from_str` at :125 with the raw model output in the error instead of falling through a match arm.
evidence: crates/triage-agent/src/main.rs:56-63 deserializes `Verdict { verdict: String, severity: String }` straight from model output, although the prompt at :71-76 defines the closed set `tp|fp|suspicious` and `low|medium|high|critical`.

crates/triage-agent/src/main.rs:415-445 matches `verdict.verdict.as_str()`: `fp` writes the verdict doc, `tp`/`suspicious` open a case, and any other value hits `other => warn!("unrecognized verdict; logging only")` — the alert is dropped with no case.
The decision-model path (:175-192) copies `Choice.choice: String` (llm-client/src/systemone.rs:165-167) verbatim without checking it is one of `VERDICT_LABELS`.

issues.summary: `Tool::execute -> Result<Value>` returns Ok for a dry run, so an unconfigured backend reads as a successful action
issues.suggestion: Return an enum from `Tool::execute`, e.g. `enum ExecOutcome { Performed(Value), DryRun { args: Value } }`, and map `DryRun` to a non-success `ToolResult` (or an explicit `skipped` field) so callers cannot mistake 'backend not configured' for 'action performed'.
evidence: crates/tool-server/src/executors/mod.rs:35-37 `dry_run()` returns `Ok(json!({"dry_run": true, "args": args}))`, and every executor falls back to it when its credential is missing (:88-91, :110-113, :145-148, :170-173, :211-214, :377-383, :408-410).
crates/tool-server/src/main.rs:193-198 maps any `Ok` to `ToolResult { ok: true, error: None }`, so the gateway (agent-core/src/gateway.rs:93-95) and the agent loop see an ordinary success.
crates/response-agent/src/main.rs:290-313 then runs `post_check` and records a rollback entry for an action that never happened.

issues.summary: Four copies of ActivityEvent (one with a different field type) plus a json! variant, consumed as untyped Value
issues.suggestion: Move a single `ActivityEvent` into `agent-protocol` (with `step: String` or a `Step` enum), use it in all five producers, and deserialize it in api-server so `terminal_step` and the SSE filter match typed fields instead of string keys.
evidence: crates/triage-agent/src/activity.rs:21 declares `pub step: &'static str` while detection/hunt/response agents declare `pub step: String` — identical JSON, incompatible Rust types, so a shared helper cannot be reused.
crates/vuln-agent/src/main.rs:120-127 publishes the same event shape from an ad-hoc `json!` block, a fifth definition.

The consumer never deserializes it: crates/api-server/src/a2a.rs:598-610 and acp.rs:201,559 walk `Value` with `v.get("workflow_run_id").and_then(Value::as_str)` and `v.get("step")`, and crates/api-server/src/stream.rs:26 relays raw `String` payloads through the broadcast channel.

issues.summary: A transport/parse failure on /invoke is synthesized as DecisionKind::Deny and persisted as a policy verdict
issues.suggestion: Keep transport failure out of `Decision`: have `invoke_tool` return `enum InvokeOutcome { Answered(InvokeResponse), Failed { error: String } }` and record `decision: null` plus a `transport_error` field, so incident records never claim a policy denial that policy never issued.
evidence: crates/response-agent/src/main.rs:212-226 builds a fake `InvokeResponse` with `Decision { kind: DecisionKind::Deny, reason: "invoke transport: …" }` for both send errors (:230) and response-parse errors (:228).
:290 treats that as `denied`, :298-307 persists `"decision": invoke.decision.kind` into `response_actions.result`, and :326-330 emits "denied by policy; recorded" to the activity feed.

issues.summary: CvssMetric fields are non-Option but parse_cve fills them with ""/0.0, and 0.0 is itself a valid CVSS score
issues.suggestion: Type the genuinely optional parts as `Option<String>`/`Option<f64>` (or have `parse_cve` skip a metric when `cvssData` is missing) and let callers decide the policy for an absent score instead of encoding absence as 0.0.
evidence: crates/connectors/src/lib.rs:813-826 declares `version: String, source: String, kind: String, vector: String, base_score: f64` with no `Option`, promising fields the NVD payload may omit.
crates/connectors/src/lib.rs:1056-1063 fills them with `unwrap_or("")` / `unwrap_or(0.0)`, so 'absent' and 'empty'/'0.0' are indistinguishable at the type level.
crates/vuln-agent/src/main.rs:100 filters `m.base_score > 0.0`, which drops a genuine CVSS 0.0 (severity None) record and cannot distinguish it from a parse default.

issues.summary: a2a/acp write protocol states as SQL literals and re-parse with lossy fallbacks instead of using the enums
issues.suggestion: Bind `TaskState::as_str()`/`RunStatus::as_str()` in the SQL statements, propagate parse failure instead of defaulting (`?` on the `Option` or `BackendError::Internal`), and add a CHECK constraint listing the enum's values so the TEXT column cannot drift from the enum.
evidence: crates/api-server/src/a2a.rs writes `'working'` (:418), `'failed'` (:442), `'canceled'` (:486-487) and `'completed'` (:337, :617) while `TaskState::as_str()` (a2a/src/task.rs:44-53) is the canonical mapping and is only used for display (:441 in acp.rs, run_event).

crates/api-server/src/a2a.rs:316 reads back with `TaskState::parse(&row.state).unwrap_or(TaskState::Submitted)`, so an unrecognised stored value becomes a live 'submitted' task that a client can re-drive.

crates/acp/src/lib.rs:172-182 maps every unknown status to `InProgress` (a completed run could be resurrected), and crates/api-server/src/acp.rs:85,452 keeps the same literals in the DDL and the cancel UPDATE.

issues.summary: Rollback plans are untyped JSON naming tools that are absent from the allowlist and never validated or executed
issues.suggestion: Introduce `struct RollbackCall { tool: ToolName, args: Value }` (or reuse `ToolCall`) built only from allowlisted names, and assert at startup that every rollback target is in `PolicyEngine::tool_names()`; if rollback execution is not planned, drop the column instead of recording unusable plans.
evidence: crates/response-agent/src/main.rs:104-129 returns `Option<Value>` built with `json!({"tool": …, "args": …})`, naming `blocklist.ip.remove`, `wazuh.active_response.unisolate_host`, `entra.user.enable`, `ad.user.enable`, `firewall.rule.remove`, `o365.email.release`, `misp.ioc.unblock`.
None of those names appears in policies/tools.yml (the allowlist ends at `siem.index.delete`), so the recorded rollback could never pass policy.
The value is written to `rollback_json` (:315-323) and no code path reads it back, so neither a type nor a test can catch the mismatch.

add.header: Acyclic layered crate graph
add.description: Contract crates (agent-protocol, a2a, acp, cvss, llm-client, connectors, http-limits) sit below core libs (agent-core, audit, enrichment-lib, policy-engine) below binaries; every internal edge is a downward path dep, so dependency direction is uniform and Cargo-enforced.

add.header: agent-protocol is the deliberate contract hub
add.description: Envelope (13 importers), tool contract (9), handoff, audit and all six routed subject constants live in one zero-dependency types crate — a hub by design, the correct shape for a message-bus platform.

add.header: Bus-mediated coupling keeps the graph shallow
add.description: Services coordinate through Envelope over NATS subjects rather than import edges; blast radius is explicit in subject names, not hidden in the dependency graph.

add.header: ACP reuses A2A machinery inside api-server
add.description: acp.rs builds on a2a.rs's AgentDef registry, publish path, build_payload and task_uuid instead of maintaining a parallel agent-facing stack.

add.header: Shared control primitives are centralized
add.description: agent-core::kill_switch_engaged is the single source for the kill file/env check across four services; http-limits serves both HTTP edges with per-service classify wiring.

add.header: Agent bootstrap is copy-paste convention, not shared runtime
add.description: tracing+clap+NATS+subscribe-spawn-envelope-span loop and emit() repeat across all agent binaries; agent-core's loop/gateway/checkpoint abstractions have no production callers, and agent_checkpoints is read but never written.

add.header: Documented bus contracts drift from runtime
add.description: services.md describes a 3-delivery DLQ, checkpoint-resume shutdowns, an activity schema with workflow_run_id, and audit_log-only cross-reads — the DLQ counter is inert, nothing checkpoints, vuln omits the field, and several extra cross-table reads exist.

add.header: connectors is a single-file leaf hub
add.description: All external-stack clients (OpenSearch, TheHive, MISP, Wazuh, Cortex, Shuffle, NVD) share one 990-LOC lib.rs imported by ~7 crates — a proportionate shared boundary but the highest fan-in leaf.

add.header: Crate-per-domain-capability layout
add.description: Each of the 21 workspace members names a security-operations capability (per-role agents, policy-engine, connectors, audit, cvss, http-limits, enrichment-lib, protocol crates); there is no util/misc/god crate, so the top level reads as the domain map rather than as history.

add.header: Spec types separated from transport
add.description: a2a/acp hold wire types and (for a2a) the transport-agnostic dispatcher plus a TaskBackend trait, while api-server owns HTTP and persistence; agent-protocol holds the internal contract. A reader can tell which crate is allowed to know about HTTP.

add.header: Uniform service binary skeleton
add.description: Six binaries share one shape — clap Config with env-backed args, tracing init, a Deps struct, a subscribe-or-cron loop — and each module header lists its routes or subjects, so moving between services costs almost nothing.

add.header: Allowlist-keyed tool registry
add.description: The Tool trait is keyed by the policies/tools.yml name, build_registry covers the whole allowlist, and missing_executors is a startup sanity check — the policy file and the dispatch table cannot drift apart silently.

add.header: Repo root mirrors the domain
add.description: Top-level directories (crates, apps/console, policies, detection-content, bas, playbooks, evals, infra, scripts) each own one kind of artifact, so 'where does this belong?' is answered by the tree.

add.header: Declared per-service table ownership
add.description: docs/services.md:20-23 names the owner of each Postgres table — a deliberate bounded-context rule. Treat it as intent, not fact: api-server's read model currently joins four tables it does not own.

add.header: connectors is the single adapter seam
add.description: Seven upstream clients (OpenSearch, TheHive, Cortex, MISP, Wazuh, Shuffle, NVD) plus one retry/auth helper live in one 1116-LOC crate, so a consumer that needs one client links all seven; the tradeoff buys uniform retry and auth behaviour across every integration.

add.header: policies/ mixes four unrelated inputs
add.description: tools.yml and protected-assets.yml belong to policy-engine, rate-limits.yml to http-limits, vuln-watchlist.yml to vuln-agent — one directory, three owners, and README documents only the first two.

add.header: Uniform service-binary skeleton
add.description: Every service crate follows the same shape: clap `Config` with env-backed args, a `Deps`/`AppState` struct holding shared clients, one `process`/`run_cycle`/`run_sweep` entry point, and a `#[tokio::main]` that inits tracing then connects. A developer can open any service and know where to look.

add.header: One executor plugin protocol in tool-server
add.description: All ~20 executors implement the single `Tool` trait with an `Option<Client>` field and a shared `dry_run` fallback, and are registered in one `build_registry` table. Adding a tool is one struct plus one `put` line, and the dry-run path means the registry stays exercisable without credentials.

add.header: Error strategy split by crate role
add.description: Typed thiserror enums live in the libraries that define domain failures (agent-core, llm-client, cvss, audit) while binaries and thin HTTP wrappers use anyhow. The split is consistent enough that a caller can predict whether it will get a matchable error type.

add.header: Accessor verb vocabulary held everywhere
add.description: `list_*`, `get_*`, `load_*` and `ensure_schema` mean the same thing in all 21 crates; there are no competing `fetch_`/`read_`/`find_` synonyms for the same operations, which is why the CRUD surface is predictable across crates.

add.header: Uniform test module placement
add.description: 17 files place `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` at the end of the file with no tests/ directory and no scattered inline asserts, so test coverage is discoverable by scrolling rather than by searching.

add.header: Agent crates are the convention drift island
add.description: The five agent binaries are the one family that diverges: four copy the same activity.rs while vuln-agent hand-rolls a different payload, and kill-switch, Deps-struct and span conventions are only partly shared. The rest of the workspace does not have this problem.

add.header: Two NATS access styles by delivery need
add.description: ingestion-gateway and orchestrator wrap NATS in a small facade (NatsSink for JetStream durability, NatsBus for core publish) while agents call `async_nats::Client` directly. The difference tracks durable-vs-fire-and-forget delivery rather than taste.

add.header: Library crates split on module visibility
add.description: agent-protocol and a2a expose `pub mod` submodules so callers write path-qualified imports, while agent-core and llm-client keep modules private and re-export a flat surface. Both are internally consistent; the split costs only a moment of 'which import style is this'.

add.header: Typed errors at library boundaries
add.description: Crates whose callers must discriminate failures expose thiserror enums with #[from] conversions (agent-core AgentError, llm-client LlmError, audit AuditError, cvss CvssError), while binaries use anyhow with .context(). The split follows 'can a caller match on this?' rather than crate type, so the two styles do not collide inside one path.

add.header: Uniform agent message-loop error boundary
add.description: All four agent binaries wrap envelope handling in the same `let result: anyhow::Result<()> = async { ... }.await; if let Err(e) = result { error!(...) }` shape and share an identical best-effort emit() helper, so a failing message is logged and the subscription survives without per-agent surprises.

add.header: Policy denial instead of error return
add.description: PolicyEngine::evaluate never returns Result: every failure becomes a Deny decision with a reason string. Authorization failure modes are therefore uniform and fail-closed, and callers never have to decide what to do with a policy error.

add.header: Resilience contract documented per dependency
add.description: docs/services.md:40-57 pins timeout, retry count and fallback for every dependency, and the main clients implement it (connectors send_with_retry, agent-core HttpToolGateway, tool-server fail-closed idempotency). Drift is therefore detectable by comparison instead of guesswork.

add.header: Best-effort enrichment returns Option
add.description: Enrichment providers return Option and aggregate what succeeded, because partial intel is more useful than an aborted triage. This is a deliberate null-style channel confined to one crate, not a second error strategy leaking into callers.

add.header: Two retry loops in connectors
add.description: NvdClient keeps a private retry loop (403 retried, exponential without jitter, no 15s budget) next to the shared send_with_retry used by every other client, justified by NVD's rate limit but not mentioned in the crate-level doc.

add.header: Protocol types named after their contract role
add.description: Envelope/EnvelopeKind, ToolCall/Decision/DecisionKind, ToolResult, HandoffPayload and AuditEvent mirror the docs and each field carries a doc comment, so a developer predicts the payload shape from the type name alone. This is why cross-crate work needs little code reading.

add.header: Pipeline functions named as ordered stages
add.description: detection-agent's draft_sigma -> validate_sigma -> write_pending -> to_lucene -> backtest -> promote_and_commit -> deploy_monitor sequence reads as the pipeline itself, so the order is legible from call sites instead of from comments.

add.header: Honest predicate names
add.description: is_retryable, is_terminal, is_truthy, is_uninteresting and budget_exceeded return exactly what their names claim and are used consistently, so boolean conditions read correctly without checking bodies.

add.header: Domain-standard abbreviations preserved
add.description: cvss keeps the FIRST spec's own tokens (av/ac/pr/ui/cia/m, macro_vector, max_composed) and connectors keeps NVD field names, so anyone holding the spec can map the code immediately; renaming them would break that link.

add.header: workflow_run_id is a documented wire alias
add.description: Activity events rename Envelope.correlation_id to workflow_run_id, and docs/services.md:81 defines the mapping while the console SSE feed consumes the wire name. The two names are a deliberate external contract, not vocabulary drift.

add.header: Acronyms camel-cased as single words
add.description: ThehiveClient, OpensearchClient, MispClient, NvdClient, CveRecord, CvssMetric and IocSet all treat acronyms the same way, so the workspace has one spelling rule rather than mixed TheHive/CVE variants.

add.header: Terse dependency structs are a shared convention
add.description: Every agent binary carries a `Deps` struct with fields like `os`, `pg`, `idem`, `hive`, `misp`; the shape repeats across five crates and the client type is declared on the field, so the brevity aids scanning rather than hiding meaning.

add.header: agent-protocol is the one shared contract crate
add.description: Envelope/EnvelopeKind, ToolCall/Decision/ToolResult, HandoffPayload and the SUBJECT_* constants live in one crate imported by 13 modules, so services exchange one message type instead of per-service copies. This is why cross-service changes stay local.

add.header: Tool trait pays for itself across 20+ executors
add.description: One dispatch seam (name + execute) behind a name-keyed registry, with a startup test asserting registry coverage of policies/tools.yml and a missing_executors sanity check. Adding a tool is one impl plus one put() call.

add.header: Idempotency shares one pure state machine
add.description: idempotency::next() is a pure KeyState->Claim transition used by both the Postgres and DashMap backends, so the three-state policy (absent/in_flight/complete/failed) is written once and the enum Store only dispatches storage.

add.header: Rate limiter takes policy as a function pointer
add.description: http_limits owns buckets, headers, 429 shaping and the stream semaphore; api-server and ingestion-gateway supply only a classify fn, so the two edge surfaces cannot drift on limit semantics.

add.header: PolicyEngine is concrete, not a trait
add.description: A single PolicyEngine type with one evaluate() boundary and a documented, load-bearing check order. No interface ceremony around the authorization gate, which keeps the security path auditable.

add.header: Name-discriminated executors inside the Tool trait
add.description: ProviderLookup, NvdTool, EntraUser, MispAttribute, WazuhActiveResponse, ShuffleWorkflow and DryRun each carry a name (or command) field and switch on it inside execute(), so one impl serves several allowlist names. Tradeoff: fewer types and registry entries, at the cost of string dispatch and a five-branch execute in ProviderLookup.

add.header: api-server AppState is a wide dependency bag
add.description: Eight heterogeneous fields (opensearch, pool, http, nvd, enricher, activity_tx, nats, jetstream) threaded through axum State. Standard for the framework, so the coupling cost is local to handlers rather than a layering problem.

add.header: Two protocol type families coexist
add.description: a2a (Task/Message/Part) and acp (Run/Message/MessagePart) model the same 'run an agent with messages' concept separately, and ACP converts to A2A messages at the boundary. Deliberate spec-fidelity choice, but it doubles the lifecycle code.

add.header: Workspace dependency inheritance as the default
add.description: All 22 external dependencies are declared once in [workspace.dependencies] (Cargo.toml:32-59) and consumed with `.workspace = true`, so a version bump is normally a one-line edit and the members cannot disagree about a shared crate. This is what keeps an otherwise drifting set coherent.

add.header: One library per concern across the whole workspace
add.description: tokio is the only runtime, reqwest the only HTTP client, serde_json the only JSON codec, chrono the only date library, sha2 the only hash, dashmap the only concurrent map. There are no moment/dayjs-style pairs for a developer to choose between, and fastrand is deliberately used for jitter instead of pulling rand.

add.header: Acyclic internal dependency graph enforced by Cargo
add.description: Every internal edge is a path dependency pointing down the layer stack (agent-protocol -> llm-client -> agent-core -> agent crates; tool-server -> policy-engine/cvss/audit/connectors) and there are no dev-dependency cycles, so Cargo itself guarantees no import cycle can appear.

add.header: Small lock-backed dependency closure
add.description: 367 packages for 21 crates and ~12.7k LOC, Cargo.lock resolves offline against the manifests, and every requirement is a caret range with no git or wildcard specs. Transitive duplication (syn, hashbrown, rand, webpki-roots) is upstream-driven rather than self-inflicted.

add.header: Thin dev-dependency surface
add.description: Only tokio (for #[tokio::test]) in a2a, llm-client and policy-engine and tower (for ServiceExt) in http-limits. No mock or assertion framework is pulled in, so test tooling adds no production weight.

add.header: Two protocol crates with overlapping type shapes
add.description: a2a and acp each own a serde/schemars type set because they model different wire protocols (Agent2Agent vs Agent Communication Protocol); the overlap is intentional, not duplicated dependency purpose.

add.header: MSRV declared once at workspace level
add.description: rust-version = "1.80" lives in [workspace.package] (Cargo.toml:30) rather than being repeated per crate; 11 of 21 members inherit it, the rest omit the field entirely (see the no_dependency_policy_gate finding).

add.header: Heavy validator confined to one crate
add.description: jsonschema 0.30 (the heaviest single addition, with referencing/fancy-regex/fraction) is used only by policy-engine at lib.rs:255,281 to validate tool argument schemas, so its cost does not propagate to the other 20 crates.

add.header: Guard-clause-first function openings
add.description: Twelve executors and both task loaders open with `let ... else { return ... }` instead of nesting, so the happy path is the unindented body. This is the dominant local style and it holds across crates, which is why single functions are easy to read even where duplication is high.

add.header: Pure state-machine transition shared by backends
add.description: Idempotency's three-state rules live once in `next(&KeyState, fingerprint) -> Claim` and both the Postgres and DashMap backends call it, so storage differences never fork the semantics. This is the model the ACP/A2A task-state code does not follow.

add.header: Named resilience constants with rationale
add.description: Retry counts, wall-clock budgets and backoff caps are named constants whose doc comments carry the reasoning (connectors CALL_BUDGET, gateway BACKOFF_CAP_MS, idempotency TTL). Readers get the contract without reverse-engineering literals.

add.header: Small-utility duplication across crates
add.description: b64url, ratelimit::build and lowercase-hex encoding exist as byte-identical or near-identical copies in separate crates because there is no shared leaf utility module. Each copy is individually correct, so the cost surfaces only when one needs to change.

add.header: Refactor residue left in hot paths
add.description: A few statements no longer do anything but still read as if they do (policy-engine's no-op drop, triage's allow(dead_code) OpensearchClient, idem_key's serde round-trip). They are leftovers from edits that removed the need, and each misleads a reviewer for a moment.

add.header: agent-protocol single-sources the message contract
add.description: Envelope, ToolCall, Decision, ToolResult, HandoffPayload and every ares.* subject except activity live in one crate, and envelope.rs is the most-imported file in the workspace (13 importers). This is why the wire shapes agree even where the adapters do not.

add.header: ACP reuses the A2A dispatch seam
add.description: crates/api-server/src/acp.rs:262-265 calls a2a::build_payload/publish/task_uuid and shares the a2a::AGENTS registry instead of copying dispatch, showing the team consolidates a seam once it is named.

add.header: Tool-invoke idempotency is an explicit, fail-closed seam
add.description: The three-state claim protocol is documented as a table (tool-server/src/idempotency.rs:1-19), the gateway retries only allow-verdict retryable results (agent-core/src/gateway.rs:93-95), and store errors fail closed rather than double-executing.

add.header: Boundary contracts are documented where they are defined
add.description: The 'HTTP 200 carries the verdict' rule (tool-server/src/main.rs:5-6), the retry/backoff budget (agent-core/src/gateway.rs:10-17) and the load-bearing policy check order (policy-engine/src/lib.rs:311-313) are stated at the seam, so the intent is recoverable even when a caller ignores it.

add.header: Transport adapters are deliberately outside the protocol crate
add.description: agent-protocol carries message types only, so each service writes its own publish and invoke glue. This is the structural reason the same seam appears three to six times.

add.header: agent-core seams are library-shaped and bypassed by the binaries
add.description: ToolGateway, CheckpointStore and AgentLoop are only used inside agent-core; api-server reads agent_checkpoints with raw SQL and re-creates the table that checkpoint.rs documents as its own, so the declared seam and the real one diverge.

add.header: Connectors are intentionally thin
add.description: connectors/src/lib.rs:1-7 states that caching and semantic retries are the caller's job, which explains why callers reach for raw HTTP when a verb is missing rather than extending the client.

add.header: Subject namespace has no single owner
add.description: ares.activity is redeclared per agent and outside agent-protocol, so the orchestrator's ares.* wildcard overlaps subjects it does not own and cannot distinguish envelope traffic from event traffic.

add.header: Trait-based stub seams in unit tests
add.description: a2a and agent-core tests inject in-memory implementations (`Stub: TaskBackend`, `EchoGateway: ToolGateway`, `InMemoryCheckpointer`, `MockProvider`) instead of mocking HTTP, so agent-loop and JSON-RPC tests assert behaviour and stay stable when transports change. This is why the 68 existing tests are cheap to maintain.

add.header: Injectable clock in rate limiter
add.description: http-limits takes `now: Instant` as a parameter (lib.rs:195, 353) so burst, refill and idle-purge tests are deterministic without sleeps. The only genuinely timing-sensitive subsystem is therefore tested without timing risk.

add.header: No snapshot or golden-file assertions
add.description: Every assertion compares an explicit value or pattern match (e.g. exact argv vectors in executors/openshell.rs, reference CVSS scores in cvss/v40.rs). There is no snapshot overuse to unwind, so test failures point at behaviour rather than at formatting churn.

add.header: Policy gate tested against real policy data
add.description: policy-engine tests load `../../policies` and assert deny-by-default, forbidden CIDRs, protected assets, blast radius, cooldown, approval and the kill file. The YAML is treated as the contract, so editing the security policy intentionally requires touching the tests.

add.header: Coverage concentrated in library crates, not binaries
add.description: All 19 tested files are `lib.rs` modules or helper modules; every service `main.rs` (triage, response, detection, hunt, vuln, orchestrator, ingestion-gateway, bas-runner) has zero tests. New logic added to a binary therefore lands outside the suite by default.

add.header: Concrete HTTP clients block agent tests
add.description: connectors exposes concrete clients (Opensearch, TheHive, Cortex, MISP, Wazuh, NVD) with no trait, so triage/response/detection `process()` cannot be exercised without network. The trait seams that exist (LlmProvider, ToolGateway, CheckpointStore, TaskBackend, Tool) stop at the connector boundary.

add.header: Policy test suite reads ambient environment
add.description: policy-engine's tests inherit `ARES_KILL_SWITCH` through `kill_switch_engaged`, so an exported variable in the developer shell or CI turns nine passing assertions into failures with misleading reasons.

add.header: Test strategy documented ahead of implementation
add.description: evals/policy_tests.md specifies 19 denial rows and evals/README.md specifies precision/recall replay, but run.sh only validates JSONL format. The intent is captured; the executable half is missing, which is why coverage gaps read as unfinished work rather than unknown requirements.

add.header: ACP surface is the house-style reference
add.description: acp crate defines one typed Error{code,message,data} with named code constants and every /acp handler routes through a single acp_err helper, so the ACP surface is predictable from one example. Copying this shape for the rest of api-server is the cheapest path to coherence.

add.header: JSON-RPC error codes centralized in a2a::rpc
add.description: All A2A error codes live as constants with a BackendError->code mapping and a single dispatch entry, each path covered by tests. Adding a method cannot invent a new error shape.

add.header: Uniform connector constructor and retry contract
add.description: Every external-system client is new(base_url, auth) with one shared send_with_retry (429/502/503/504 + connect/timeout, 15s budget), so a developer learns the retry semantics once for all seven integrations.

add.header: Async Result-typed trait boundaries
add.description: Tool, ToolGateway, CheckpointStore, LlmProvider and TaskBackend all declare async methods returning Result with documented failure modes, so the pluggable seams are honest even where the concrete services are not.

add.header: Registry keyed by policy allowlist with startup check
add.description: build_registry keys executors by allowlist name and missing_executors plus a test guarantees every policies/tools.yml entry resolves, so tool-name drift fails loudly instead of silently at invoke time.

add.header: Closed vocabularies as String at agent boundaries
add.description: LoopOutcome.stop_reason and the triage Verdict fields are free-form Strings matched with literals, while a2a/acp model equivalent state with enums. Likely a consequence of parsing LLM JSON quickly; unifying them would remove the stringly-typed comparisons but touches every agent.

add.header: Three Message types across protocol crates
add.description: llm_client::Message (role enum + content), a2a::Message (Role + Part list, text() -> Option<String>) and acp::Message (string role + parts, text() -> String) coexist. Each mirrors a different wire spec, but the shared name and divergent text() return type make cross-protocol code read ambiguously.

add.header: Tool executors take untyped JSON args by design
add.description: The single Tool trait signature execute(&Value) keeps the registry homogeneous across 25+ tools at the cost of per-tool key guessing; that tradeoff is reasonable, but it needs the policy args_schema to be the published contract.

add.header: Always-200 /invoke contract
add.description: tool-server deliberately answers 200 with the verdict in the body so callers never parse status codes for policy outcomes; documented in the service header and docs/services.md. The remaining defect is that consumers do not all honor it.

add.header: Single deny-by-default tool gate
add.description: PolicyEngine::evaluate runs a fixed, documented check order (kill switch, allowlist, autonomy, args_schema, forbidden_args, protected assets, blast radius) and returns Deny for anything absent from tools.yml, so a reviewer can predict the verdict path for any tool call.

add.header: Hash-chained audit of every verdict
add.description: tool-server appends every decision (allow, deny, approval_required) to audit_log with args_sha256 and prev_hash/hash chaining, and approval outcomes are audited with the approver as actor — the audit trail is designed to be tamper-evident rather than advisory.

add.header: Executors re-validate independently of policy
add.description: Executors do not trust the policy verdict: OpenShellExec re-checks a command allowlist and a shell-metacharacter denylist and fails closed when the sandbox is unreachable, giving genuine defense in depth at the last hop.

add.header: Router-level rate limiting on both edge services
add.description: api-server and ingestion-gateway both apply the same http_limits middleware at the router, with tier thresholds in policies/rate-limits.yml, so a new route is metered by default instead of opting in.

add.header: Authorization gaps documented with a probe
add.description: docs/services.md carries an OWASP API Top 10 table naming each unauthenticated path and scripts/api-security-check.sh probes them, so the gaps are known and re-testable rather than folklore — documentation does not substitute for the missing middleware, but it keeps the backlog honest.

add.header: No inbound authentication anywhere
add.description: All three HTTP services are anonymous by design today; rate-limit keys are the peer IP with an explicit 'until authentication lands' note, so every authorization decision currently applies to a tool name, never to a principal.

add.header: Single owner Postgres role, no RLS
add.description: Every service connects with one DATABASE_URL owner role and creates its own tables ad hoc, so there is no per-service database boundary and audit_log is writable by the services it audits.

add.header: Actor identity is a caller-supplied string
add.description: ToolCall.actor travels in the request body and is ignored by the policy engine, so audit attribution reflects what the client claimed, not who connected.

add.header: Webhooks intentionally unauthenticated
add.description: /webhook/wazuh and /webhook/generic accept anonymous POSTs by documented design and are metered on the ingest tier; this is the one trust boundary the codebase states openly rather than implying protection it lacks.

add.header: Comments carry constraints, not narration
add.description: Inline comments record load-bearing facts a reader cannot infer: the fixed order of policy checks (policy-engine/src/lib.rs:311-313), the 72h idempotency TTL being longer than the DLQ replay window (idempotency.rs:27-29), and the 15s retry budget (connectors/src/lib.rs:63-72). This is why the comment ratio is high without being noise in the security core.

add.header: Degraded mode expressed once, not per call
add.description: Missing credentials resolve through a single `dry_run(args)` helper (executors/mod.rs:35) and audit failure degrades to one log line (tool-server/src/main.rs:82-99) instead of per-executor null checks. This keeps the executor file free of defensive sprawl.

add.header: No entry/exit or object-dump logging
add.description: The workspace has 5 `debug!` calls total, all on cache-hit or poller-skip paths; `info!`/`warn!` mark decisions and degraded paths. Logging adds signal rather than ceremony.

add.header: Bounded retry logic is documented in place
add.description: connectors/src/lib.rs:65-123 and agent-core/src/gateway.rs:1-90 spell out MAX_RETRIES, the jitter formula and the per-call budget, so the resilience behaviour is reviewable without reading the loop.

add.header: missing_docs lint drives field-level doc bloat
add.description: `#![warn(missing_docs)]` in agent-protocol, a2a, acp, agent-core, llm-client and audit forces a doc line on every public item, producing restatements like `/// Agent name.` above `name: String`. The bloat is a lint artifact, not an authorship style, so it is cheap to fix at the source.

add.header: Agent scaffolding duplicated per binary
add.description: Five agent binaries each carry their own ActivityEvent, emit helper and NATS subscribe loop; the copies have already diverged (triage's `&'static str` step, vuln-agent's event without workflow_run_id). New agent features must be applied in five places until this is shared.

add.header: agent-core is speculative infrastructure
add.description: AgentLoop, HttpToolGateway, CheckpointStore and Budgets are exported but never constructed outside the crate; only kill_switch_engaged and the AgentState types are consumed. This leaves the checkpoint read paths in api-server unreachable and the gateway retry contract unenforced.

add.header: No deprecated symbols anywhere
add.description: No `#[deprecated]` attribute exists in the workspace and no active code calls a deprecated alias; superseded paths were deleted rather than kept as shims, so a developer never has to check whether a symbol is the old one.

add.header: axum 0.8 route migration complete
add.description: Every route in crates/api-server/src/main.rs:283-325 uses `{param}` syntax and main.rs:386 builds the router in a test specifically to catch reintroduced 0.7 `:param` strings, so the migration cannot silently regress.

add.header: Single NVD API 2.0 client
add.description: crates/connectors/src/lib.rs:802-1037 is the only NVD integration (one base URL, one rate limiter, one retry budget); no 1.0 endpoint or second parser survives, so CVE data has one shape.

add.header: Rate limiting consolidated in http-limits
add.description: Both edge services consume the shared crate (api-server/src/main.rs:360-365, ingestion-gateway/src/main.rs:139-146) and their local ratelimit.rs files only map request paths to tiers, so the earlier per-service limiter story is fully replaced.

add.header: ACP reuses the A2A publish path
add.description: crates/api-server/src/acp.rs:16-18 and :244-265 build runs on a2a::AGENTS, a2a::build_payload and a2a::publish instead of copying transport, so adding a second protocol did not create a second envelope path.

add.header: thiserror in libraries, anyhow in binaries
add.description: Typed thiserror enums sit at library boundaries (agent-core/src/error.rs:4, llm-client/src/error.rs:4, cvss/src/lib.rs:15, audit/src/lib.rs:31) and binaries use anyhow; this is deliberate layering, not the drift the mechanical pattern pair suggests.

add.header: Legacy rate-limit headers kept on purpose
add.description: http-limits emits the `x-ratelimit-limit/remaining/reset` trio and calls it legacy in its own docs (lib.rs:13,238) and in docs/services.md:103-109; it is a deliberate client-facing contract, not stale residue.

add.header: ACP resume endpoint is an intentional stub
add.description: api-server/src/acp.rs:422-424 always rejects resume with `invalid_input` because ARES agents never emit `awaiting`, and says so; a documented, bounded spec-completeness exception.

add.header: Documented ownership map at repo root
add.description: README.md's 'Repo layout' table and docs/services.md's 'Contexts and ownership' table name the owner of every top-level path and database table, so a new developer can navigate by contract rather than by search. This is the main reason the crate-level layout reads as intentional.

add.header: agent-core private modules with public facade
add.description: crates/agent-core/src/lib.rs declares all 7 modules private and re-exports AgentLoop, Budgets, Checkpointer, ToolGateway and kill_switch_engaged, so internal file placement can change without touching the 5 consumer crates.

add.header: Per-service crates split by responsibility
add.description: ingestion-gateway (main/pollers/nats_sink/ratelimit), orchestrator (main/dedupe/nats_bus), cvss (lib/v31/v40/lookup_table) and a2a (lib/card/rpc/task) all keep 2-5 cohesive files per crate, which is the pattern the monolith crates should follow.

add.header: Shared mechanism crates for edge concerns
add.description: http-limits owns the limiter and each service supplies only a `classify` function (api-server/ratelimit.rs, ingestion-gateway/ratelimit.rs), and agent-protocol owns the envelope/tool contracts with 13 and 9 importers — sharing happens where the mechanism is identical and varies only by policy.

add.header: Four single-module monolith crates
add.description: connectors (1189 LOC), tool-server executors/mod.rs (816), policy-engine (779) and enrichment-lib (579) hold ~27% of the workspace LOC with no submodule boundary, so the crate is the only navigable unit inside them.

add.header: Cross-cutting contracts duplicated instead of placed
add.description: The activity event, the kill switch and the policies directory have no owning module, so they are re-implemented per crate (6, 3 and 5 copies respectively) and have already diverged in wire shape and fail-closed semantics.

add.header: Module names shadow sibling crates in api-server
add.description: api-server's `mod a2a` and `mod acp` collide with the workspace crates of the same name, forcing `::a2a::task::Message` at acp.rs:244 and making `a2a::` ambiguous to readers.

add.header: Zero mutable module-scope state
add.description: The workspace has no `static mut`, `lazy_static`, `once_cell`, `thread_local`, build.rs or ctor hooks; the only two module-level statics are a lazily compiled regex set and a lazily built HTTP client, both pure and order-independent. A developer can import any crate with no import-time side effects.

add.header: Explicit state injection via AppState and Deps
add.description: Every service builds its state in `main` and passes `Arc<AppState>`/`Arc<Deps>` into handlers and spawned tasks, so there is no global singleton whose creation order matters across modules - the reason this dimension has no boot-order races.

add.header: Env reads deferred to call-time getters
add.description: `llm_client::fast_model()`/`strong_model()` keep the default model as a documented const and read the override when called; all four consumers call the getters and only a unit test touches the const, so no stale import-time snapshot is propagated.

add.header: Live kill-switch re-read is intentional
add.description: The kill switch is deliberately re-evaluated from env plus the kill file on every check instead of being snapshotted at boot, which is the correct behaviour for an operator safety control - the defect is the duplicated implementation, not the freshness.

add.header: Two config resolution planes
add.description: Boot-time `ConnectorConfig::from_env()` (empty-string filtering) coexists with per-request `env::var` reads in raw-HTTP helpers and executor bodies, so the same credential can resolve differently and be re-read at request time.

add.header: Schema DDL lives in service binaries
add.description: Seven inline `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` blocks sit in service mains rather than owner crates, api-server creates agent-core's `agent_checkpoints`, and `audit_log` has no initializer anywhere - making cross-service boot order an implicit deployment prerequisite.

add.header: Process CWD is an implicit boot input
add.description: `detection-content/active`, `bas/scenarios`, `policies` and `playbooks` are repo-relative constants resolved against the working directory with silent empty-result fallbacks, so services only behave correctly when launched from the repository root.

add.header: Pure transition shared by both idempotency stores
add.description: crates/tool-server/src/idempotency.rs:110-135 defines KeyState->Claim as a pure function that both the Postgres and DashMap stores call, so the three-state claim protocol is specified once and storage stays a detail. Copy this shape when a rule must hold across two backends.

add.header: Policy evaluation is a numbered check ladder
add.description: crates/policy-engine/src/lib.rs:344-440 runs nine labelled checks in a documented, load-bearing order with early returns, so a reviewer can audit authorization by reading top to bottom. New checks get a number, not a new branch elsewhere.

add.header: One function per pipeline stage
add.description: crates/detection-agent/src/pipeline.rs keeps each detection stage (draft, validate, write, convert, backtest, promote, deploy, audit) in its own function and composes them in run_cycle, which is why that pipeline reads as a checklist rather than a monolith.

add.header: Registry built from one table with a startup completeness test
add.description: crates/tool-server/src/executors/mod.rs:674-797 registers executors in one place and pairs it with missing_executors plus a test asserting every policies/tools.yml name resolves, so adding a tool has one obvious edit site and a failing test if it is forgotten.

add.header: Shortcuts are labelled where they are taken
add.description: Deliberate limits are documented at the point of use (detection-agent/src/pipeline.rs:108-110 naive Lucene mapping, hunt-agent/src/main.rs:71-72 hit scoring, a2a.rs:483 cancel gap, approvals.rs:11-13 in-memory queue), so a reader learns the boundary without git archaeology.

add.header: Protocol DTO crate stays transport-free
add.description: crates/a2a splits spec DTOs (card, task), the JSON-RPC dispatcher and the TaskBackend trait, so dispatch is unit-tested against an in-memory stub and knows nothing about Postgres or NATS. That is the right seam; the api-server module above it is where the duplication currently lives.

add.header: One module per vendor inside the connectors crate
add.description: crates/connectors/src/lib.rs groups seven HTTP clients under section banners with the same new(base_url, auth) shape. Coherent today, but it is a single 1189-line file, so a new vendor is an append rather than a new module.

add.header: Each agent binary owns its own Deps and main loop
add.description: Every agent defines a private Deps struct and consume loop instead of sharing a runtime; this is why activity/emit/subscribe scaffolding is copied per crate and why agent-core's AgentLoop is unused. Treat it as a deliberate tradeoff only if the shared runtime is deleted.

add.header: Known-gap docstrings instead of silence
add.description: Modules routinely state what they deliberately do not do (unpriced max_cost_usd, in-memory approvals lost on restart, cancel not observed by in-flight agents, resume always rejecting). This makes the boundary of each contract visible without reading implementations, and is why the defects that remain stand out.

add.header: Wire types documented against their spec
add.description: a2a/task.rs and acp/lib.rs document the exact spec JSON spelling (`sessionId`, `kind`, kebab-case statuses) and the tests assert the serialized shape, so the wire contract is verifiable rather than implied.

add.header: Shared constants back shared contracts
add.description: ToolResult's retryable marker (RETRYABLE_FIELD) and the a2a JSON-RPC error codes are single constants consumed by both producer and consumer, which is why those contracts cannot drift.

add.header: Terminal step names are an implicit contract
add.description: api-server's terminal_step hardcodes step strings ('close', 'handoff', 'kill_switch', 'done', 'deployed', 'rejected') emitted by four agent crates that each define their own ActivityEvent; a rename on either side silently stops SSE streams from closing and blocks the task-state write-back.

add.header: Per-crate ActivityEvent copies
add.description: Each agent crate defines its own ActivityEvent; three are identical and triage's differs in field type (`step: &'static str` vs String). The wire shape matches today, but there is no shared type enforcing it.

add.header: Numbered guard-clause policy pipeline
add.description: PolicyEngine::evaluate_inner is a flat sequence of numbered early returns whose order is documented as load-bearing, so a reviewer can verify the deny-by-default ordering without following nested branches.

add.header: Pure idempotency transition function
add.description: idempotency::next encodes the claim state machine once and both the Postgres and DashMap backends route through it, keeping a table-driven invariant instead of two divergent implementations.

add.header: Large files are flat, not tangled
add.description: The structural hotspots (connectors, tool-server executors, api-server a2a) are long because they are repetitions of one client method or one handler shape; their control flow is shallow, so file size does not translate into logic confusion here.

add.header: Kill-switch logic implemented twice
add.description: agent_core::kill_switch_engaged and PolicyEngine::kill_switch_engaged duplicate the truthy-env parsing and kill-file check with different path resolution ($POLICIES_DIR/kill vs {policy_dir}/kill), so the two can drift on the same operator control.

add.header: Per-agent ActivityEvent copies diverge
add.description: Each agent crate carries its own activity.rs; the step field is &'static str in four of them and String in response-agent, so the shared SSE event shape is only kept aligned by hand.

add.header: Status enums keep a second spelling table
add.description: TaskState and RunStatus each expose as_str/parse alongside their serde renames, giving two sources of truth for the wire spelling (RunStatus::parse even relies on the wildcard for "in-progress").

add.header: Protocol enums carry explicit wire conversions
add.description: a2a's `TaskState` and acp's `RunStatus` pair a serde enum with `as_str`/`parse`, and `Part`/`Step`/`Directive` are `#[serde(tag=...)]` enums, so legal states and payload shape are compiler-checked rather than convention-checked. This is why protocol-layer work feels safe while domain vocabulary does not.

add.header: No unwrap/expect in production paths
add.description: Every `unwrap`/`expect` in crates/ sits inside a `#[cfg(test)]` module except seven `LazyLock<Regex>` initializers and one reqwest builder call, so typed Options are not routinely short-circuited and a reader can trust `?`-based flows.

add.header: Per-crate thiserror error enums
add.description: LlmError, CvssError, AuditError, AgentError and BackendError are exhaustive enums with `#[from]` conversions, so callers match variants instead of inspecting strings and failure modes stay typed at each boundary.

add.header: Tool arguments are deliberately untyped JSON
add.description: `Tool::execute(&Value) -> Result<Value>` takes free-form args because the caller is an LLM; the actual contract is the per-tool `args_schema` in policies/tools.yml, compiled and enforced by the policy engine. The dynamism is a tradeoff, not an oversight.

add.header: SQL rows re-parse enums from TEXT by hand
add.description: Protocol state columns are TEXT, so api-server re-parses with `TaskState::parse`/`RunStatus::parse`; the pattern is intentional (no sqlx enum mapping is wired) but a2a returns `Option` and acp silently defaults, so the same job has two different contracts.
